# Sheet engine

A tiny spreadsheet engine for the planning tool of a harbour office. `sheet(source)` takes the text of a sheet (one cell per line), evaluates every cell and returns the values as text. Numbers are integers; there are no decimals, strings or dates.

## Sheet text

Lines are separated by `\n`; line numbers count from 1. Leading and trailing blanks (spaces, tabs) of a line are ignored; a line that is then empty, or starts with `#`, is skipped. Every other line is `CELL = FORMULA`: the text before the **first** `=` (blanks trimmed) must be a valid cell name, the text after it (blanks trimmed, possibly empty) is the formula. A later line for the same cell replaces the earlier one.

A **cell name** is a column letter `A` to `J` followed by a row number `1` to `99` written without a leading zero (`A1`, `J99`, `C10`). If a line is not of the form `CELL = FORMULA` (no `=`, or an invalid cell name) the whole result is `error: line N` for the first such line (`N` is its line number) and nothing else is evaluated.

## Formulas

Tokens (blanks between tokens are ignored): **integers** (ASCII digits); **references** (a run of ASCII letters followed by one or more digits, e.g. `B7`, `K12`, `a1`); the operators `+ - * / %`, parentheses, and `:`. Anything else is a syntax error.

```
formula := sum
sum     := product { ('+' | '-') product }
product := unary { ('*' | '/' | '%') unary }
unary   := '-' unary | atom
atom    := INTEGER | REF | '(' formula ')'
```

The whole formula must be consumed. Any violation is a **syntax error**, and the value of that cell is `#SYN` (the rest of the sheet is unaffected). Without functions in this engine, a function name is a syntax error too. A `REF:REF` range is not available here; the `:` token makes the formula a syntax error.

## Values and errors

Every value is an integer whose absolute value is **at most 9999999**; an integer literal, or a result of `+`, `-`, `*` that is larger in absolute value, is the error `#NUM` (unary minus never leaves the range). An integer literal with more than nine digits is also `#NUM`.

* A **reference** whose text is not a valid cell name (`K1`, `A0`, `A100`, `a1`, `A01`) is `#REF`. A reference to a valid cell that has no line is `0`.
* **Errors propagate**: if an operand (or a function argument) evaluates to an error, the whole operation has that error. Operands are evaluated left to right and evaluation stops at the first error, so the leftmost failing operand decides which error is reported.
* **Division**: `/` is only allowed when the division is exact; a non-zero remainder gives `#DIV` (`6 / 3 = 2`, `7 / 2` is `#DIV`); `%` is the remainder with the sign of the dividend (`-7 % 2 = -1`). Dividing by 0 (with `/` or `%`) is `#DIV`.
* **Cycles**: the value of a cell is `#CYC` when computing it needs the value of that same cell, directly or through other cells, following only the references that are actually evaluated (every reference in the formula is evaluated). A cell that merely reads a `#CYC` cell gets `#CYC` through normal error propagation. A self-reference is a cycle.

## Result

One line `CELL = VALUE` for every cell that has a line (even when its formula is empty or erroneous), in row order: by row number, then by column letter (`A1`, `B1`, `A2`, ...). `VALUE` is the decimal integer (a leading `-` for negatives, no `+`) or the error text (`#SYN`, `#REF`, `#DIV`, `#NUM`, `#CYC`). Lines are joined with `\n`, no trailing newline; a sheet without cells gives the empty text. An empty formula is `#SYN`.

## Interface

Implement this function in `src/sheetcalc.js`:

```
function sheet(source)  // returns a string; exported with module.exports
```

* `source`: the sheet text
* returns the evaluated sheet as text.

All inputs and the result are plain strings. Invalid input is reported *inside the result text* as the rules in this document say; the function itself never throws, panics or exits.

## Examples

Sheet:

```
A1 = 12
A2 = 30
B1 = A1 + A2 * 2
```

Result:

```
A1 = 12
B1 = 72
A2 = 30
```

Sheet:

```
A1 = 7
B1 = A1 * (A2 + 3)
# A2 is empty
C1 = B1 / 4
```

Result:

```
A1 = 7
B1 = 21
C1 = #DIV
```

Sheet:

```
A1 = 2
A2 = A1 + B1
B1 = A2
```

Result:

```
A1 = 2
B1 = #CYC
A2 = #CYC
```

Run the visible tests with `node --test test/*.test.js`.

```
formula := sum
sum     := product { ('+' | '-') product }
product := unary { ('*' | '/' | '%') unary }
unary   := '-' unary | atom
atom    := INTEGER | REF | RANGE | NAME '(' [ formula { ',' formula } ] ')' | '(' formula ')'
RANGE   := REF ':' REF
```

The whole formula must be consumed. Any violation is a **syntax error**, and the value of that cell is `#SYN` (the rest of the sheet is unaffected). A range `REF:REF` may appear only as a direct argument of `TOTAL`, `MIN`, `HIGHEST`, `MEAN`, `COUNT`; anywhere else it is a syntax error (this includes arguments of any other function, even an unknown one).

## Values and errors

Every value is an integer whose absolute value is **at most 9999999**; an integer literal, or a result of `+`, `-`, `*`, the aggregate sum and `SNAP` that is larger in absolute value, is the error `#NUM` (unary minus never leaves the range). An integer literal with more than nine digits is also `#NUM`.

* A **reference** whose text is not a valid cell name (`K1`, `A0`, `A100`, `a1`, `A01`) is `#REF`. A reference to a valid cell that has no line is `0`.
* **Errors propagate**: if an operand (or a function argument) evaluates to an error, the whole operation has that error. Operands are evaluated left to right and evaluation stops at the first error, so the leftmost failing operand decides which error is reported.

* **Cycles**: the value of a cell is `#CYC` when computing it needs the value of that same cell, directly or through other cells, following only the references that are actually evaluated (every reference in the formula is evaluated). A cell that merely reads a `#CYC` cell gets `#CYC` through normal error propagation. A self-reference is a cycle.

## Functions

Function names are upper-case and matched exactly; a name that is not in the table is `#NAME` (when the call is evaluated). A wrong number of arguments is `#ARG`, detected **before** any argument is evaluated. Arguments are evaluated left to right.

| function | meaning |
|---|---|
| `TOTAL(a, b, ...)` | sum of all values (0 if there are no values) |
| `MIN(a, b, ...)` | smallest value (`#NUM` if there are no values) |
| `HIGHEST(a, b, ...)` | largest value (`#NUM` if there are no values) |
| `MEAN(a, b, ...)` | sum of the values divided by their number, using the division rule above (`#NUM` if there are no values) |
| `COUNT(a, b, ...)` | how many values there are |

The aggregate functions take **one or more** arguments (no argument: `#ARG`). Each argument is a formula or a range. A formula argument contributes one value. A range `X1:Y2` covers the rectangle of cells between the two corners, whichever corner comes first (`B3:A1` is the same as `A1:B3`); it contributes the value of every cell **that has a line**, in row order (row by row, columns A to J within a row); cells without a line contribute nothing. A corner that is not a valid cell name makes the range `#REF` (it is checked when the range is evaluated). `#NUM` for an oversized sum is checked on the final sum only.

| function | meaning |
|---|---|
| `ABS(x)` | absolute value |

## Result

One line `CELL = VALUE` for every cell that has a line (even when its formula is empty or erroneous), in row order: by row number, then by column letter (`A1`, `B1`, `A2`, ...). `VALUE` is the decimal integer (a leading `-` for negatives, no `+`) or the error text (`#SYN`, `#REF`, `#DIV`, `#NUM`, `#CYC`, `#NAME`, `#ARG`). Lines are joined with `\n`, no trailing newline; a sheet without cells gives the empty text. An empty formula is `#SYN`.

## Interface

Implement this function in `src/Sheetcalc.java` (class `Sheetcalc`, default package):

```
public static String sheet(String source)
```

* `source`: the sheet text
* returns the evaluated sheet as text.

All inputs and the result are plain strings. Invalid input is reported *inside the result text* as the rules in this document say; the function itself never throws, panics or exits.

## Examples

Sheet:

```
A1 = 12
A2 = 30
B1 = A1 + A2 * 2
```

Result:

```
A1 = 12
B1 = 72
A2 = 30
```

Sheet:

```
A1 = 4
A2 = 9
A3 = 2
B1 = TOTAL(A1:A3)
B2 = HIGHEST(A1:A3) - MIN(A1:A3)
```

Result:

```
A1 = 4
B1 = 15
A2 = 9
B2 = 7
A3 = 2
```

Sheet:

```
A1 = 2
A2 = A1 + B1
B1 = A2
```

Result:

```
A1 = 2
B1 = #CYC
A2 = #CYC
```

start.tests/test_sheetcalc.py:
import os
import sys
import unittest

sys.path.insert(0, os.path.join(os.path.dirname(os.path.abspath(__file__)), "..", "src"))
from sheetcalc import sheet  # noqa: E402

CASES = [
    (("A1 = 12\nA2 = 30\nB1 = A1 + A2 * 2",), "A1 = 12\nB1 = 72\nA2 = 30"),
    (("A1 = 4\nA2 = 9\nA3 = 2\nB1 = TOTAL(A1:A3)\nB2 = MAX(A1:A3) - MIN(A1:A3)",), "A1 = 4\nB1 = 15\nA2 = 9\nB2 = 7\nA3 = 2"),
    (("A1 = 2\nA2 = A1 + B1\nB1 = A2",), "A1 = 2\nB1 = #CYC\nA2 = #CYC"),
]


class Cases(unittest.TestCase):
    def test_cases(self):
        for args, want in CASES:
            with self.subTest(args=args):
                self.assertEqual(sheet(*args), want)


if __name__ == "__main__":
    unittest.main()

start.README.md:
# Sheet engine

A tiny spreadsheet engine for the planning tool of a harbour office. `sheet(source)` takes the text of a sheet (one cell per line), evaluates every cell and returns the values as text. Numbers are integers; there are no decimals, strings or dates.

## Sheet text

Lines are separated by `\n`; line numbers count from 1. Leading and trailing blanks (spaces, tabs) of a line are ignored; a line that is then empty, or starts with `#`, is skipped. Every other line is `CELL = FORMULA`: the text before the **first** `=` (blanks trimmed) must be a valid cell name, the text after it (blanks trimmed, possibly empty) is the formula. A later line for the same cell replaces the earlier one.

A **cell name** is a column letter `A` to `J` followed by a row number `1` to `99` written without a leading zero (`A1`, `J99`, `C10`). If a line is not of the form `CELL = FORMULA` (no `=`, or an invalid cell name) the whole result is `error: line N` for the first such line (`N` is its line number) and nothing else is evaluated.

## Formulas

Tokens (blanks between tokens are ignored): **integers** (ASCII digits); **references** (a run of ASCII letters followed by one or more digits, e.g. `B7`, `K12`, `a1`); **function names** (a run of ASCII letters followed by `(`); the operators `+ - * / %`, parentheses, `,` and `:`. Anything else is a syntax error.

```
formula := sum
sum     := product { ('+' | '-') product }
product := unary { ('*' | '/' | '%') unary }
unary   := '-' unary | atom
atom    := INTEGER | REF | RANGE | NAME '(' [ formula { ',' formula } ] ')' | '(' formula ')'
RANGE   := REF ':' REF
```

The whole formula must be consumed. Any violation is a **syntax error**, and the value of that cell is `#SYN` (the rest of the sheet is unaffected). A range `REF:REF` may appear only as a direct argument of `ADDUP`, `LOWEST`, `MAX`, `AVERAGE`, `COUNT`; anywhere else it is a syntax error (this includes arguments of any other function, even an unknown one).

## Values and errors

Every value is an integer whose absolute value is **at most 9999999**; an integer literal, or a result of `+`, `-`, `*`, the aggregate sum and `SNAP` that is larger in absolute value, is the error `#NUM` (unary minus never leaves the range). An integer literal with more than nine digits is also `#NUM`.

* A **reference** whose text is not a valid cell name (`K1`, `A0`, `A100`, `a1`, `A01`) is `#REF`. A reference to a valid cell that has no line is `0`.
* **Errors propagate**: if an operand (or a function argument) evaluates to an error, the whole operation has that error. Operands are evaluated left to right and evaluation stops at the first error, so the leftmost failing operand decides which error is reported.
* **Division**: `/` truncates towards zero and `%` is the matching remainder (it has the sign of the dividend: `-7 / 2 = -3`, `-7 % 2 = -1`). Dividing by 0 (with `/` or `%`) is `#DIV`.
* **Cycles**: the value of a cell is `#CYC` when computing it needs the value of that same cell, directly or through other cells, following only the references that are actually evaluated (every reference in the formula is evaluated). A cell that merely reads a `#CYC` cell gets `#CYC` through normal error propagation. A self-reference is a cycle.

## Functions

Function names are upper-case and matched exactly; a name that is not in the table is `#NAME` (when the call is evaluated). A wrong number of arguments is `#ARG`, detected **before** any argument is evaluated. Arguments are evaluated left to right.

| function | meaning |
|---|---|
| `ADDUP(a, b, ...)` | sum of all values (0 if there are no values) |
| `LOWEST(a, b, ...)` | smallest value (`#NUM` if there are no values) |
| `MAX(a, b, ...)` | largest value (`#NUM` if there are no values) |
| `AVERAGE(a, b, ...)` | sum of the values divided by their number, using the division rule above (`#NUM` if there are no values) |
| `COUNT(a, b, ...)` | how many values there are |

The aggregate functions take **one or more** arguments (no argument: `#ARG`). Each argument is a formula or a range. A formula argument contributes one value. A range `X1:Y2` covers the rectangle of cells between the two corners, whichever corner comes first (`B3:A1` is the same as `A1:B3`); it contributes the value of every cell **that has a line**, in row order (row by row, columns A to J within a row); cells without a line contribute nothing. If a covered cell has an error value the aggregate fails with that error (the first one in that order). A corner that is not a valid cell name makes the range `#REF` (it is checked when the range is evaluated). `#NUM` for an oversized sum is checked on the final sum only.

| function | meaning |
|---|---|
| `ABSOLUTE(x)` | absolute value |

## Result

One line `CELL = VALUE` for every cell that has a line (even when its formula is empty or erroneous), in column order: by column letter, then by row number (`A1`, `A2`, `B1`, ...). `VALUE` is the decimal integer (a leading `-` for negatives, no `+`) or the error text (`#SYN`, `#REF`, `#DIV`, `#NUM`, `#CYC`, `#NAME`, `#ARG`). Lines are joined with `\n`, no trailing newline; a sheet without cells gives the empty text. An empty formula is `#SYN`.

## Interface

Implement this function in `src/Sheetcalc.java` (class `Sheetcalc`, default package):

```
public static String sheet(String source)
```

* `source`: the sheet text
* returns the evaluated sheet as text.

All inputs and the result are plain strings. Invalid input is reported *inside the result text* as the rules in this document say; the function itself never throws, panics or exits.

## Examples

Sheet:

```
A1 = 12
A2 = 30
B1 = A1 + A2 * 2
```

Result:

```
A1 = 12
A2 = 30
B1 = 72
```

Sheet:

```
A1 = 4
A2 = 9
A3 = 2
B1 = ADDUP(A1:A3)
B2 = MAX(A1:A3) - LOWEST(A1:A3)
```

Result:

```
A1 = 4
A2 = 9
A3 = 2
B1 = 15
B2 = 7
```

Sheet:

```
A1 = 2
A2 = A1 + B1
B1 = A2
```

Result:

```
A1 = 2
A2 = #CYC
B1 = #CYC
```
